method: GitHub Actions run creation to final job completion, including queue and cache work. Each run is one sample, not a guaranteed duration.
notes: Baseline uses the previous successful main revision, with uncached Docker builds and existing Cargo caches.

The initial run creates new job/cache scopes. Every Rust/native/specification suite passed, but the fixture image failed because its two synthetic identity include files were excluded from the build context. The aggregate gate failed correctly. Gateway dependencies and image layers were exported successfully.

The follow-up restores the two exact fixture inputs, shares application compilation between the two images, removes CI dev/test debug symbols while keeping debug assertions and the release profile unchanged, and persists the temporary Rust specification harness target.

Two intermediate pushes were superseded before completion. Their cancelled jobs exposed incomplete immutable Cargo caches created by cache-on-failure. The final configuration saves only successful jobs and uses fresh version-three Cargo keys.

The successful final-profile run restores the Docker chef and dependency layers, recompiles both application binaries in a shared stage (370 seconds), and creates complete Cargo caches. This is not the fully warm comparison.
See tasks/036-optimize-ci-runtime.md for the subsequent fully warm and documentation-only measurements. JSON validation reports intentionally require full CI.
